channel: payload-builders/_threads/select latest not highest from a relay_builder when making repeated getExecutionPayloadBid
searchText: hey y’all wanted to start a thread since prysm and lodestar have draft PRs out for requesting repeated bids and there’s some longer term consequences worth discussing now rather than later - Prysm’s PR https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/17723 - Lodestar’s PR https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/10425 bringing this up since Mev-Boost and Commit-Boost have offered this feature for a while in PBS ~ I really would push back on implementing it where the BN selects the **highest** instead of the **latest** bid from a relay/builder. While selecting the highest makes sense intuitively for proposer revenue, it breaks cancellations which arguably is worse in the long term with centralization consequences. I’m neither so will let the <@&1458826346896687229> and relays chime in but my understanding is: Option A) If BN’s default to selecting highest - builders lose ability to cancel -> expected to bid lower / more conservatively - lower execution rewards for proposers - larger node operators have the reputation to be trusted to respect cancellations - they will earn more than the average smaller untrusted operators - smaller operators will start receiving just one *repeated* conservative bid regardless of how many times they query, also defeating the purpose of the PRs Option B) Then assuming BNs default to selecting latest - builders continue to bid assuming cancellations are respected - sophisticated operators can defect by forking a client or sidecar to select the highest bid - this behavior is observable retroactively and builders/relays can adjust i.e., stop sending them bids the difference is option A “lowers the tide” for all, then rewards larger operators for free. whereas option B punishes the sophisticated operators trying to defect so the ask is if BN’s are going to offer this feature to implement it as *latest-only* In prysm everything is configurable, so selecting the "latest bid" is completely equivalent to just delaying the request and requesting only once

hey y’all wanted to start a thread since prysm and lodestar have draft PRs out for requesting repeated bids and there’s some longer term consequences worth discussing now rather than later
- Prysm’s PR https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/17723
- Lodestar’s PR https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/10425

excerpts.author: jvranek
excerpts.content:
bringing this up since Mev-Boost and Commit-Boost have offered this feature for a while in PBS ~

I really would push back on implementing it where the BN selects the **highest** instead of the **latest** bid from a relay/builder. While selecting the highest makes sense intuitively for proposer revenue, it breaks cancellations which arguably is worse in the long term with centralization consequences.

I’m neither so will let the  <@&1458826346896687229> and relays chime in but my understanding is:

Option A) If BN’s default to selecting highest
- builders lose ability to cancel -> expected to bid lower / more conservatively
- lower execution rewards for proposers
- larger node operators have the reputation to be trusted to respect cancellations
- they will earn more than the average smaller untrusted operators 
- smaller operators will start receiving just one *repeated* conservative bid regardless of how many times they query, also defeating the purpose of the PRs

Option B) Then assuming BNs default to selecting latest 
- builders continue to bid assuming cancellations are respected
- sophisticated operators can defect by forking a client or sidecar to select the highest bid
- this behavior is observable retroactively and builders/relays can adjust i.e., stop sending them bids

the difference is option A “lowers the tide” for all, then rewards larger operators for free. whereas option B punishes the sophisticated operators trying to defect

so the ask is if BN’s are going to offer this feature to implement it as *latest-only*

excerpts.content: In prysm everything is configurable, so selecting the "latest bid" is completely equivalent to just delaying the request and requesting only once
